finding.claim: wipe() never enforces the OWNER role check, so any authenticated caller can irreversibly wipe any tenant. requireRole's boolean result is discarded.
finding.source: The User u parameter (name and roles) supplied by the caller of wipe(), which per the route comment on line 24 is POST /tenants/{t}/wipe. The caller can supply any User value whose roles set lacks "OWNER", including an empty set.
finding.sink: repo.wipe(tenant) at src/Admin.java:27, a destructive tenant-wide operation.

trace.note: Route comment: POST /tenants/{t}/wipe maps to this method.
wipe(User u, String tenant) accepts the caller-supplied user and tenant.
requireRole(u, "OWNER") is called. It returns a boolean that is not checked, so execution always continues.
requireRole only returns u.roles().contains(role). It does not throw, as the javadoc on line 13 states.
repo.wipe(tenant) runs for every caller, with no role check.

finding.guards_checked: The only guard in wipe() is requireRole on line 26, which is a non-enforcing predicate whose result is ignored. No other check exists in the method. The sibling export() on line 32 uses checkRole, which does throw, so the non-enforcing call on line 26 is a defect and not a deliberate design. No caller code, filter, or interceptor exists in the repository to enforce the role before wipe() is reached.

verdict.guard_found: None effective. The only check in wipe() is requireRole(u, "OWNER") at src/Admin.java:26, a non-throwing boolean predicate (src/Admin.java:14-15) whose result is discarded, so repo.wipe(tenant) at line 27 runs unconditionally. The throwing variant checkRole (src/Admin.java:18-22) is used by export() at line 32 but not by wipe(). A grep of the repository finds no other role check, filter, or interceptor.
verdict.reason: Every trace line matches the code: wipe() at src/Admin.java:25-27 discards the boolean from requireRole at line 26 and always calls repo.wipe(tenant), while the sibling export() at line 32 uses the throwing checkRole. Any authenticated caller who lacks OWNER can reach this route, and nothing in the repository blocks that; the caveat is that the repo does not show how the route builds the User argument, so the caller scope depends on code outside this repository.

finding.claim: wipe() and export() accept an arbitrary tenant string and never check that the caller belongs to that tenant. A caller holding OWNER in one tenant could wipe or export a different tenant (cross-tenant access). Verdict: PLAUSIBLE, since the file does not show whether roles are scoped per tenant.
finding.source: The caller-supplied tenant String parameter (line 25 for wipe, line 31 for export) together with the User record, whose roles are a bare Set<String> with no tenant identifier (line 4).
finding.sink: repo.wipe(tenant) at src/Admin.java:27 and repo.export(tenant) at src/Admin.java:33, a destructive operation and a data-exfiltration operation on tenant data.

trace.note: User(String name, Set<String> roles) has no tenant field, so role membership is not tied to any tenant.
wipe(User u, String tenant) takes the tenant from the caller and does not compare it to anything in u.
export(User u, String tenant) has the same shape.
repo.wipe(tenant) runs on the caller-chosen tenant.
repo.export(tenant) runs on the caller-chosen tenant.

finding.guards_checked: No tenant-membership check exists in either method. checkRole on line 19 tests only the role name and not the tenant. The repository does not define how roles are stored or scoped, so this cannot be confirmed from this file alone. If roles are global, any OWNER can act on any tenant. If the caller layer already binds the user to the tenant, this finding does not apply.

verdict.guard_found: Line 26 requireRole(u, "OWNER") in wipe() returns a bool that is discarded, so it blocks nothing. Line 32 checkRole(u, "OWNER") in export() throws on a missing role, but it checks only the role name and never the tenant. No tenant-membership check exists in either method, and the User record (line 4) carries no tenant.
verdict.reason: Every trace line matches the file (Admin.java:4, 25, 27, 31, 33), and no tenant check exists in either method, but whether roles are tenant-scoped depends on the caller layer, which is not in the provided code, so the cross-tenant claim cannot be decided here. The file does show a separate in-file bug the candidate missed: the requireRole result at Admin.java:26 is discarded, so wipe() has no role check at all (any User reaching it can wipe any tenant), which should be filed on its own.
